sourceToScriptToScreen.centralPoint: A viewing reward faces outside availability

sourceToScriptToScreen.plannedScreen: Observed enemy clear→reward→dialogue; online viewing relation is abstract MC, not recorded analytics.

sourceToScriptToScreen.retainedClaim: Dialogue often advances line by line; continuous movie segments can benefit from partial skip or fast-forward.

sourceToScriptToScreen.centralPoint: Adapt viewing control to actual habits
sourceToScriptToScreen.retainedClaim: Playback services permit faster viewing; the wish to show carefully authored scenes does not remove the value of playback controls.
sourceToScriptToScreen.addedExplanation: Independent abstract playback timeline; no borrowed Netflix/lesson screenshot. Avoid inserting a platform-behavior tutorial.
sourceToScriptToScreen.plannedScreen: General playback control, no claim Hades/ACNH has an unobserved fast-forward mode.

sourceToScriptToScreen.retainedClaim: Allow skipping all movies including credits. A first save/playthrough is not proof this person has never watched the scene.

sourceToScriptToScreen.plannedScreen: Whole skip and confirmation are general design diagrams; credits rule retained.

sourceToScriptToScreen.retainedClaim: Quick Time Event means a timed button input during a directed sequence; abrupt required inputs can frustrate viewers.

sourceToScriptToScreen.addedExplanation: Define QTE canonically, cue→time window→input→visible result. Preserve original caution and conclude by returning to why/when control helps the cinematic role.
sourceToScriptToScreen.plannedScreen: Source example also abstract. MC shows timed mechanism, no fabricated commercial game QTE.
